newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada bonds end weaker with U.S., spreads narrow.
newsitem.headline: Canada bonds end weaker with U.S., spreads narrow.

text.p: Canadian bonds closed weaker in quiet trade on Monday, with spreads to U.S. long bonds narrowing, as concern about tomorrow's key U.S. employment data weighed on prices, dealers said.

"It's nothing more than the U.S. market. Spreads across the curve have tightened today and the currency has done better," said a trader at one Toronto brokerage. "There's fear in the U.S. market of a potential bad employment costs index tomorrow and nothing more."
Canada's 30-year bond fell C$0.10 to C$107.15 to yield 7.379 percent.
The U.S. 30-year benchmark bond fell 20/32 to yield 6.94 percent. The spread between benchmark bonds narrowed to 44 basis points from 49 basis points at Friday's close.

Dealers said the Canadian market mirrored concern among U.S. investors that U.S. employment cost index data for the fourth quarter due on Tuesday will indicate accelerating inflation. U.S. Federal Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan last week voiced concerns about rising U.S. wages.
The decline in Canadian bond prices was tempered somewhat by today's strong performance in the Canadian dollar, analysts said.
Canada's dollar ended firmer at C$1.3442 (US$0.7440) on Monday from Friday's close of C$1.3485 (US$0.7416) in fairly thin trading, dealers said.
In other prices, the Government of Canada's 7.0 percent bond due 2006 fell C$0.06 to C$101.87 to yield 6.735 percent. The U.S. 10-year bond fell 10/32 to yield 6.67 percent.
The spread between the benchmark bonds narrowed to seven basis points from nine basis points at Friday's close.
The three-month cash T-bill traded with a yield of 2.87 percent against the U.S. bill yielded 5.18 percent.
